owner: CC — CC gates writes to this intention; the host setting is the box's, applied by sudo.
intention: Every Linux box that runs cairn's tester allows unprivileged user namespaces under AppArmor (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0, persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/60-uu-userns.conf), so bwrap can build the tester's instance seal and `cairn test --exec` runs instead of refusing.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akienasus after its reinstall: `cairn test --exec` refused 'the instance seal is not confirmed ... kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 ... bwrap cannot build a sandbox', so every proof that re-runs an instrument under the seal (codemother's verdict re-run in test_deposit, and clause_6 of 2b3d842bc118) read red on this box and green on akiendelllinux. The Dell held /etc/sysctl.d/60-uu-userns.conf from the UU era; the reinstall dropped it, and nothing in either repo installs it, so the knowledge lived only on one disk. Ubuntu 24.04+ ships the restriction at 1 by default.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing is proved without the seal a hollow build cannot pass, and the seal needs this host setting) and the host-seam class's reason to exist: the intentions folder is the seed a bare box regrows from.
ticket: see CairnCommons/tickets/ (cast 2026-11-12, title 'every box that runs the tester allows unprivileged user namespaces')
cost: Lifting the AppArmor restriction lets any unprivileged process create a user namespace again, which is the kernel's pre-24.04 default. Ubuntu added the restriction to narrow the kernel attack surface reachable from an unprivileged user. Accepted on the house boxes, matching akiendelllinux since UU.

apply.note: Complete recipe. A mind on a fresh Ubuntu box needs nothing from either repo but this block. Needs sudo.
apply.3_bwrap: bwrap must be installed (sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap); the tester's seal shells out to it.
apply.absent_key: On a kernel with no /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns (pre-24.04, or AppArmor off) nothing restricts userns and steps 1-2 are skipped; sysctl -p would otherwise print an unknown-key error.

verify.command: test "$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" = 0 && grep -qx 'kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0' /etc/sysctl.d/60-uu-userns.conf && cd ~/dev/src/cairn && bin/cairn test --exec true --timeout 30
verify.green: exit 0: the live value is 0, the persisted file holds the line, and the tester's sealed exec runs a command
verify.horizon: after every OS reinstall or release upgrade, and at a box's first cairn start; a reinstall is the measured drift that bore this node

measured.saw: akienasus: /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1, /etc/sysctl.d held only 99-zram.conf and README.sysctl; `cairn test --exec` refused for want of bwrap's sandbox
measured.how: cat the proc key, ls /etc/sysctl.d, bin/cairn test cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_deposit.py

measured.saw: akiendelllinux: the key reads 0, set by /etc/sysctl.d/60-uu-userns.conf
measured.how: ssh akiendelllinux.local cat the proc key and grep -r userns /etc/sysctl.d

measured.saw: after apply on akienasus: the key reads 0, test_deposit green, `bin/cairn test --exec true --timeout 30` exit 0
measured.how: the verify command above, run on akienasus
